messages.text: Man City sponsor's 2015 statement raises questions about appeal strategy

metadata.summary: Manchester City’s strategy in their bid to clear their name after being found guilty of breaking more than 100 of the Premier League's rules has been brought into question by a statement their main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to the US government in 2015.
metadata.content: Man City appeal: Club's strategy brought into question by 2015 statement main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to US government | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City appeal: Club's strategy brought into question by 2015 statement main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to US government Man City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City deny all charges and have lodged an appeal against the verdict; City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 breaches in February 2023 By Zinny Boswell and Kaveh Solhekol Friday 2 October 2026 23:00, UK Manchester City’s strategy in their bid to clear their name after being found guilty of breaking more than 100 of the Premier League's rules has been brought into question by a statement their main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to the US government in 2015. Sky Sports News understands that City are expected to argue as part of their appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's majority owners, Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG). However, a statement Etihad submitted to the US Departments of Commerce, Transportation and State in May 2015 appears to contradict this explanation. messages.text: Djokovic battles through fitness issues to produce resilient China Open comeback

metadata.summary: Novak Djokovic again appeared to struggle with fitness issues as he came from behind to avoid a second-round exit to world No 104 Yunchaokete Bu at the China Open on Friday.
metadata.content: China Open and Japan Open: Novak Djokovic, Aryna Sabalenka and Naomi Osaka all advance, as Katie Boulter knocked out | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content China Open and Japan Open: Novak Djokovic, Aryna Sabalenka and Naomi Osaka all advance, as Katie Boulter knocked out Novak Djokovic sealed a second-round comeback win in Beijing as Naomi Osaka and Aryna Sabalenka both advanced; Katie Boulter was once again beaten by Karolina Muchova watch ATP Japan Open and WTA/ATP China Open this week live on Sky Sports Friday 2 October 2026 19:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Djokovic extended his winning run at the China Open to 31 matches Novak Djokovic again appeared to struggle with fitness issues as he came from behind to avoid a second-round exit to world No 104 Yunchaokete Bu at the China Open on Friday. The Serbian went 1-0 down before he was taken to a tiebreak in the second set. But Djokovic dug deep to claim the final set and cap off a resilient 4-6 7-6(7-2) 6-2 comeback victory over the Chinese wildcard, and extend his record winning streak at the China Open to 31 matches. messages.text: Jordan handles Piers Morgan 'sledging' to move into contention

metadata.summary: Matthew Jordan shot a seven-under 65 to move into contention at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship despite having to put up with Piers Morgan's verbal jousting.
metadata.content: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: Matthew Jordan moves into contention with Casey Jarvis leading by one | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: Matthew Jordan moves into contention with Casey Jarvis leading by one Matthew Jordan survives 'sledging' from outspoken television presenter Piers Morgan to move into contention at Alfred Dunhill Links; South African Casey Jarvis leads by one on 11 under after a 67 at Kingsbarns Friday 2 October 2026 19:54, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day two of the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship. Matthew Jordan shot a seven-under 65 to move into contention at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship despite having to put up with Piers Morgan's verbal jousting. The Royal Liverpool member is looking for his first DP World Tour win in his 183rd tournament and he shrugged off the good-natured criticism from the television presenter - his amateur playing partner for the team part of the event - to card six birdies and an eagle at Carnoustie. His one mishap was a bogey at the ninth, his final hole, but he got to 10 under and into a four-way tie for second place. messages.text: Price edges last-leg epic as Wade beats Van Veen to book Humphries semi

metadata.summary: Gerwyn Price survived three match darts to beat Jonny Clayton in a final-leg thriller at the World Grand Prix, as James Wade emphatically dumped out Gian van Veen in Leicester.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix: James Wade thrashes Gian van Veen to book Luke Humphries semi-final after Gerwyn Price edges thriller | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix: James Wade thrashes Gian van Veen to book Luke Humphries semi-final after Gerwyn Price edges thriller Luke Humphries beat Niels Zonneveld to book a semi-final meeting with James Wade, while Nathan Aspinall will play Gerwyn Price in the last four; watch the World Grand Prix semi-finals live on Saturday from 8pm on Sky Sports+ and 8.30pm on Sky Sports Main Event Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Friday 2 October 2026 23:08, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gerwyn Price snatched victory from the jaws of defeat as compatriot Jonny Clayton missed three match darts in their World Grand Prix quarter-final Gerwyn Price survived three match darts to beat Jonny Clayton in a final-leg thriller at the World Grand Prix, as James Wade emphatically dumped out Gian van Veen in Leicester. Price battled back from two sets down in an absorbing all-Welsh contest at the Mattioli Arena, where he won six of the next seven legs to level the match before Clayton edged ahead in a dramatic final set. Clayton missed a match dart to win the set in straight legs and saw Price drag the contest into a last-leg decider, where 'The Ferret' wasted two more match-winning darts to allow his compatriot to snatch victory and a semi-final spot. messages.text: Mariota to start for Commanders in London as Daniels ruled out

metadata.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota will get his second start in place of the injured Jayden Daniels on Sunday when his side face the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium - live on Sky Sports.
metadata.content: NFL London Games 2026: Marcus Mariota to start for Washington Commanders vs Indianapolis Colts as Jayden Daniels ruled out | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NFL London Games 2026: Marcus Mariota to start for Washington Commanders vs Indianapolis Colts as Jayden Daniels ruled out Marcus Mariota will make his second start of the NFL season in London as he steps in for injured quarterback Jayden Daniels for Washington Commanders' clash against Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday; watch live at 2pm on Sky Sports NFL Friday 2 October 2026 20:36, UK Image: Marcus Mariota will start for the Washington Commanders against the Indianapolis Colts in London, with Jayden Daniels ruled out Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota will get his second start in place of the injured Jayden Daniels on Sunday when his side face the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium - live on Sky Sports. Head coach Dan Quinn announced the decision on Friday after practice at the team's hotel accommodations outside London. Daniels returned to practice this week after dislocating his elbow in Week Two against the Dallas Cowboys. He's been wearing a protective brace and had expressed no concerns about further damage, but the Commanders will hold him out for at least one more game.
